newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-RIEGLER LEADS AFTER SLALOM FIRST LEG.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-RIEGLER LEADS AFTER SLALOM FIRST LEG.

text.p: New Zealand's Claudia Riegler led a tightly-bunched field after the first leg of a women's World Cup slalom on Sunday.
Riegler, the winner of the season's first two slaloms, twisted her way through the 51 gates on the sun-drenched Barguns course in a time of 38.55 seconds.
She is pursued by a group of eight skiers, all less than half a second behind.

Reigning World Cup slalom champion Elfi Eder of Austria, who is still looking for her first win of the season, is just 17 hundredths of a second adrift with 38.72, followed by France's Patricia Chauvet with 38.85.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, who can wrap up the slalom World Cup title with a good result, is fourth with 38.86.
The slalom, which also counts for a combined event with Saturday's downhill here, is the last race before the world championships get underway on Monday in Sestriere, Italy.
